summary: Terese Tse Bartholomew worked in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. She earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.

Teruji Ishizu was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926) and taught Takushu Sugimoto. His academic career included posts at Tohoku University (~1940–1967), Keio University (~1967–1972), Tokyo, Nihon, and Aichi Universities.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz worked in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Universities of Florida, Ceylon, and Virginia (PhD 1991), Florida State, Banaras Hindu, and Cornell. She held posts at Virginia, Florida State (1993), and IUPUI (~1991–2001).

Tetsuei Sato specialized in Buddhist studies and studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He held professorial posts at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (attested 1972), and was later named professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (attested 1972–1976).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his education at Taisho University, where he studied under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1877–1880), Heidelberg (~1884–1887), and Leipzig (~1887–1890). He taught Taiken Kimura and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1882–1890) and Toyo University.

Tetsuo Otani studied at Waseda and Komazawa Universities. In Buddhist studies, he held posts at Komazawa University (~1980–1990; 2002–2006), Tomakomai Komazawa (2006–2007), Tsuru (2013–2016), Tohoku Fukushi (2015–2019), and Peking University.
Tetsuo Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who was educated at Shizuoka University. He served as an assistant professor at Otani University from circa 1971 to 1978.

Tetsuro Watsuji studied at the University of Tokyo (~1909–1912), working in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He taught Yasuo Yuasa and held posts at Hosei, Toyo, Kyoto (~1925–1934), Tokyo (~1934–1949), Otani, and Ryukoku Universities.
Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held academic posts at Utrecht University, where he was attested in 1989 and later recognized as Professor Emeritus by 2000.
Thanon Chitkament is a researcher in the field of history and archaeology. Academic research was conducted under the guidance of V. D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1842–1847). He served as Privatdozent there (1850), Professor of Sanskrit at Edinburgh (1862), and Professor at Bonn (1875–1889), succeeding Christian Lassen.

Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1824–1826). He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881), teaching numerous notable scholars.
Theodor Bloch was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University (~1888–1892) under Ernst Windisch and later pursued studies under Georg Bühler (~1894–1895).

Theodor Goldstücker worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg, Bonn, and under Burnouf, von Bohlen, Lassen, and Rosenkranz. He later served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London and University College London (~1852–1872).

Theodor Nöldeke specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Göttingen (under Theodor Benfey), Vienna, Berlin, and Leiden. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1861–1864) and the University of Kiel (~1864–1872).
Theodore Dwight Woolsey was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who studied at Hopkins School and Yale College (~1816–1820). He also taught Edward Elbridge Salisbury.

Theodore Gabriel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen and served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.

Theodore Stcherbatsky was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. A member of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1931), he taught Otto Rosenberg and Eugène Obermiller.
Theophil Gubler worked in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jacob Wackernagel and completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel in 1903.
